purpose: Show one shared GTM Brain knowledge chain projected into Marketing, Sales, and CX assets.

sources.title: Cross-team GTM knowledge fragmentation synthesis
sources.content_summary: Illustrative synthesis describing duplicated research, inconsistent messaging, and weak cross-team reuse.

evidence.statement: Reviewed team retrospectives describe Marketing, Sales, and CX storing customer and market learning in separate workflows, leading to repeated research and inconsistent reuse.
evidence.confidence_basis: The illustrative synthesis combines more than one team perspective but does not represent production research.

audiences.name: Cross-functional GTM leader
audiences.role: Leader accountable for alignment across Marketing, Sales, and CX
jobs_to_be_done: Create one reliable view of customer, market, product, and field knowledge.
Keep team messaging and decisions aligned without erasing source ownership.
pain_points: Teams repeat research because prior work is difficult to find or trust.
Messages drift because evidence, claims, and approved language are mixed together.
desired_outcomes: Reuse shared knowledge across team workflows.
Trace important messages and assets to current evidence and owners.
objections: We already have separate tools for each team.
A shared layer may become another stale repository.
success_criteria: Each team can contribute knowledge through a common contract.
Marketing, Sales, and CX assets reference the same governed records.

insights.statement: When GTM knowledge remains in team-specific workflows, teams duplicate research and adapt messages without a shared evidence or approval context.
insights.confidence_basis: The illustrative evidence supports the operating problem, while implementation outcomes remain unmeasured.
gaps: No production baseline for duplicated research or message drift is included.
No business outcome is attributed to the proposed operating model.

claims.statement: A shared governed knowledge layer lets Marketing, Sales, and CX reuse the same source-linked evidence, insights, claims, and approved messages in team-specific assets.
claims.confidence_basis: The claim describes the intended operating model shown by the repository; it does not claim measured adoption or business impact.
allowed_uses: Explain the GTM Brain operating model.
Frame the relationship between shared knowledge and team assets.
prohibited_uses: Do not claim measured time savings, revenue impact, adoption, or production scale.
Do not imply that the skeleton automatically ingests, generates, or publishes content.

messages.text: Capture customer, market, product, and field learning once, govern it as shared knowledge, and reuse it across Marketing, Sales, and CX assets.
restrictions: Do not present the skeleton as an automated or production system.
Do not add unsupported business outcomes or customer adoption claims.

assets.title: Shared GTM knowledge layer content brief
assets.purpose: Explain the shared knowledge operating model to a cross-functional GTM leader.
restrictions: Do not claim measured time savings, revenue impact, production scale, or automated ingestion.
known_gaps: No production implementation or performance baseline is represented.

assets.title: Separate tools objection handling
assets.purpose: Provide a governed response when a GTM leader asks why a shared layer is needed alongside team systems.
restrictions: Do not say that GTM Brain replaces systems of record or automatically eliminates duplicate work.
known_gaps: No implementation-specific integration or adoption evidence is included.

assets.title: Cross-team knowledge handoff signal summary
assets.purpose: Show how CX can use the shared chain to summarize handoff and expectation signals for all GTM teams.
restrictions: Do not present illustrative themes as actual customer feedback or measured prevalence.
known_gaps: No authorized customer quote, support record, onboarding note, or adoption signal is included.

reviews.rationale: The message accurately describes the static operating model, retains the shared-knowledge boundary, and explicitly excludes automation and outcome claims.
resolved_gaps: Clarified that reuse occurs through shared records and team templates.
unresolved_gaps: No production implementation or measured business result is represented.
